builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Cannot Wait to Verify: Parallel Drafting to Eliminate Verifier Idle Time in Speculative Decoding
summary: It replaces sequential draft generation in speculative decoding with parallel evaluation of transformer layers from a shared hidden state, using hidden-state divergence to accept or correct layer-wise draft states. The cost is added scheduling and consistency-check logic plus possible small accuracy degradation, though no architecture modification or retraining is required. It can fail if hidden-space divergence does not predict token-level acceptance, if correction overhead erodes the drafting speedup, or if results do not transfer to the reader's model, workload, or single-GPU serving setup.
rationale: It addresses verifier idle time without retraining, but the production benefit depends on acceptance behavior, model/task transfer, and integration with an existing speculative-decoding stack.
technique: Parallel layer-wise drafting for speculative decoding

claims.statement: It replaces sequential draft generation in speculative decoding with parallel evaluation of transformer layers from a shared hidden state, using hidden-state divergence to accept or correct layer-wise draft states. The cost is added scheduling and consistency-check logic plus possible small accuracy degradation, though no architecture modification or retraining is required. It can fail if hidden-space divergence does not predict token-level acceptance, if correction overhead erodes the drafting speedup, or if results do not transfer to the reader's model, workload, or single-GPU serving setup.
The paper reports up to 1.65x speedup of the drafting stage with minimal accuracy degradation while preserving speculative-decoding performance.
